title: Constant quotient-complex and normalized reduction data
statement: For a scheme $W$, a commutative ring $R$ and an ideal $I\subseteq R$, use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], inverse limits [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit], sheaf tensor products and change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], the ordinary constant-coefficient pro-etale pullback and its adjunction [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], the constant module realization [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] and inverse-system towers [def-weil-inverse-system]. Define the quotient rings $A_n=R/I^{n+1}$ ($n\ge0$), the tower of constant ring sheaves $\underline{A_n}_W$ with its consecutive quotient maps, and its limit $B_W$. Define extension of scalars of module sheaves along a map of ring sheaves (the sheafified sectionwise change of rings) and its local pure tensor sections, the constant scalar-module realization with its constant sections, the finite complexes $D_{W,n}^\bullet=\underline{A_n}_W\otimes_{\underline R_W}\underline{P^\bullet}_W$ with the original differential, and the image of a section under the unit of the ordinary pullback. Define strict quotient-transition data $D_{W,n+1}^\bullet\to D_{W,n}^\bullet$ normalized on local tensor generators by $a\otimes p\mapsto q_{n+1,n}(a)\otimes p$, and the resulting strict tower of complexes over $\underline R_W$. For bounded finite-projective scalar complexes $P^\bullet$ define the completed complexes $B_W\otimes_{\underline R_W}\underline{P^\bullet}_W$ and reduction data: balanced finite reductions $\underline{A_n}_W\otimes_{B_W}(B_W\otimes\underline{P^\bullet}_W)\cong D_{W,n}^\bullet$, quotient units, the reduction tower of $B_W$-modules through the limit projections, and the product map of the reductions into the product of that tower, the input of the strict Roos cone [def-sf-strict-roos-functor]. Each datum comes with its normalization predicate on local tensor generators; no inverse image of $B_W$, no inverse of a coefficient map and no finite-free splitting is used.
